messages:
Alex: Dropping quick handoff thread — I'm primary until 08:00 UTC. Left the short runbook links and top remediation steps for common pages below. If you take anything, reply here so I mark it.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident #1234 | high p95 latency on text-gen-prod detected by latency-monitor (p95 > 800ms) — auto-escalated to oncall at 2024-12-02T07:42:10Z
Mira: thx Alex. is customer impact confirmed? which routes are affected?
Alex: quick summary: 3% of requests hitting model x-large are seeing p95 spikes. Most requests still succeed, errors ~0.1%, but latency spike causes user-facing slowness for streaming endpoints. Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: rdx-xl), fallback still serving rdx-large fine.
Alex: Runbook (short): https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/oncall-handoff (long) and https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/latency-p95-textgen (short cheat-sheet)
Alex: Immediate triage checklist (do these in order):
```
1) Check runtime health: `redwoodctl cluster status` and `redwoodctl runtime pods --filter=rdx-xl`
2) Inspect slow tail logs: `kubectl logs -l app=runtime,model=rdx-xl -n inference --tail=300`
3) Check autoscaler: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` and `redwoodctl autoscale status rdx-xl`
4) If KV cache pressure visible, trigger cache-evict: `redwoodctl cache evict --model rdx-xl --prefix=kv` (safe, non-disruptive)
5) If latency persists and infra CPU spiking, scale up pool or route -> rdx-large via Console or `redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --model rdx-large --reason "temp mitigation"`
```
Alex: Note: prefer cache-evict and checking batching before scaling to avoid cost. If you must scale, use burst capacity (policy: burst-ops-1) not permanent resize.
Mira: for cache-evict, any gotchas? I recall a previous evict caused short-term tail errors
Alex: Good call — evict will increase cold KV misses briefly. Do it during lower traffic if possible. If evict + fallback still fails, do a controlled rolling restart of the runtime pods for rdx-xl:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-rdx-xl -n inference
# watch:
kubectl get pods -l app=runtime,model=rdx-xl -n inference -w
```
Jon: I'm on standby for the next hour then OOO. I can't be secondary for 02:00-04:00 UTC — coverage gap there.
Alex: noted. Sam — can you cover 02:00-04:00 UTC tonight? We need a secondary in case the latency recurs.
Sam: I can take 02:00-04:00 UTC. Ping me on pager if incident fires. :+1:
Mira: if you need to failover to another region, runbook snippet:
```
1) Check model parity: Console -> Model catalog -> verify rdx-large/rdx-xl availability in eu-west
2) Update routing policy: `rwctl route set --region eu-west --route /v1/generate --model rdx-large`
3) Monitor SLOs and rollback after stabilizing.
```
Alex: Customer impact note to paste in status updates: "Some users may experience elevated latency on streaming generation (p95 ~800ms). No elevated error rates detected. Working on cache and routing mitigations; engineering oncall engaged." Use that for incident page.
Mira: saved. One more: where's the evacuation checklist for stuck GPUs? had to power-cycle a node last time.
Alex: GPU node ops: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/gpu-node-recovery — top steps: drain node (`kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`), restart host agent (`systemctl restart redwood-host-agent`), and verify kernel nv driver. If no infra access, escalate to eng-infra on-call.
incident-bot: Note: incident #1234 set to P2 and assigned to Alex as primary; status: investigating.
Sam: thanks — I'll monitor dashboards 02:00-04:00 UTC and keep this thread open for handoff.
Alex: handing off primary -> Sam at 08:00 UTC (per schedule) unless any other pages. Closing notes: mark any actions you take in this thread (cache-evict, rollout, route-change) and include command+timestamp for audit. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
